subject: redis-check-aof.c: Avoid leaking file handle if file is zero bytes (#12797)
reason: This is a pure resource-leak fix: redis-check-aof.c now calls fclose(fp) before returning AOF_CHECK_EMPTY for a zero-byte AOF file. The tool's observable behavior (exit status, stdout, stderr) is byte-identical on both builds for every input: an empty file is reported 'is empty' and the tool proceeds/exits the same way. The leaked descriptor is reclaimed at process exit and only becomes visible under file-descriptor exhaustion, which requires an impractical, environment-dependent number of empty INCR files and is non-deterministic.
